label: site
files: website/build.py, website/summary.py, tests/test_site.py, tests/test_summary.py and, for the D74 item only, tests/test_addresses.py
items: Site completion items (rulings D78 to D83; the store is the adopted combined store /home/user/hail-b5/out/combined/store, whose tile lists now carry display names in title case with ghcn_name beside them; the browser owner's round-2 reports under /home/user/hail-b5/out/b2r2/browser/ and the contract file /home/user/hail-b5/out/b2r2/browser/ref/section_data_contract.json say exactly what the browser reads). Items, in order: (1) The browser review's F1: map_data_summary writes summary.section_data per the contract file (kind.*, roof.lines.*, roof.reference_line, roof.extra, roof.held_names, roof.partial_keys, rules, words.* including report_near, span_to, county_word, nearest_station, no_miles, roof_part, roof_part_lower, tail_five_roof, tail_five_comma, kind_what, kinds, row_labels, season_rows, section_keys, extra_notes, partial_marker), from the constants and words summary._sections, _extra, _roof and build.history_view use, so the sheet's sections equal describe_summary's text with no literal in map.js; summary.rule.percent = {scale 100, decimals 1, step 0.1}; the season share rule and the unit scales in summary.rule and summary.units (D83(b)); nouns.days = ['day', 'days']; hail.joins.show_first = 10 (D83(a)); a test that every key the browser reads from the summary block, section_data included, is written. (2) D78(c): the summary and the tests show the display names as the store gives them, never re-cased; the products completion pass is rebuilding the adopted store's tile lists and stations block with title-case names and a ghcn_name key during your run: at your final run read the stations block, and if ghcn_name is present take the exact names from r0092_c0214.json for the name-case tests; if it is not yet present, write the tests to the display-name rule (title case, direction and distance tokens kept) and list the item as pending the products pass. (3) D82(c): the radar count row follows D37's rule (a zero only at 95 percent coverage, else Data unavailable with the days missing), the 'No radar estimate of 0.25 in or more' sentence only at 95 percent, and the radar maximum row shows the largest value over the days present with its coverage line; tests. (4) D74: tests/test_addresses.py near line 870 expects 'its completeness varies from county to county'. (5) The browser owner's test specs in tests/test_site.py: (a) drop the .hail-days assertion near line 1655 so the dead map.html CSS can go; (b) summary.rule.percent equals the three values; (c) share parity: the browser's sumSharePct over round(k/2192, 4) for k = 0 to 2192 equals summary._share_text, ties at k = 137, 685, 1233 and 1781 named; (d) a fixture sheet check that no rendered line holds '[missing'; (e) a static check that the joined sheet code has no '|| 10' or 'showFirst: 10'; and the browser-against-module comparison of the table, its notes and every section's text for the five cells (Billings 921,2149; Benchland 792,1998; the gate 797,1986; 753,2230; 920,1899) on the fixture and the adopted store (read map.js again before your final run; the browser owner edits it in this pass). (6) D82(d): build.history_view carries describe_joins's section lines (the freshness lines, the NCEI flood cause line, the zone-switch line, the no-county-product line with its evidence caveat, the implausible-count line) as notes of the section each part feeds, so the town page and the sheet show them alike; the browser mirrors from the same data; a test on the Billings page. (7) Whatever the round-2 site check under /home/user/hail-b5/out/b2r2/site/check.json left not done or partial in your files. (8) Run tests.test_summary (with HAIL_PARITY_STORE set to the adopted store), tests.test_site, tests.test_addresses and the full suite (tail; name every failure and whose it is); a scratch build from the adopted store with every flag to read the Billings and Benchland pages; delete the build.

label: browser
items: Browser completion items (rulings D78 to D83; the store is the adopted combined store /home/user/hail-b5/out/combined/store; the site owner writes summary.section_data, summary.rule.percent, nouns.days and hail.joins.show_first in this pass, so build against a scratch build of the current tree and, where a key is still missing, keep the missingKey placeholder and list the exact key under needed from the site owner). Items, in order: (1) histLine (near line 4996) fills indicator_unavailable with kind: spec.kind (Python writes '{kind}: {label}. {why}'); the sheet's unavailable gust line begins 'Station reading: Peak gust of 50 knots'. (2) Thousands separators through thousands(n) (helper near line 2787) in sumMissingText, sumCountText and its final return, the station-days fills and partial_missing, so the sheet and the town page print the same '1,020 days' and '1,826 days missing'. (3) D83(b): the season rule's 95 percent and the unit scales come from map.json (summary.rule's season share; summary.units.in.scale and summary.units.F.scale), replacing the literals near lines 3514, 3638, 3738, 4009, 4423, 4424, 4450, 4451 and 4574. (4) F13: the dead .hail-days, .hail-classes and .joins-* CSS in map.html goes once the site owner's test edit (5a) lands (read tests/test_site.py near line 1655 before your final run). (5) D78(c): the sheet shows station names as the store gives them (title case from the products completion pass), never re-cased. (6) D82(d): the joined sections' lines (freshness, NCEI flood cause, zone switch, the county caveat, the implausible count) render as notes of the section each part feeds, as history_view now carries them (the site owner adds them in this pass; keep the placeholder if the key is missing and list it). (7) Checks: python -m unittest tests.test_site -k HailJoinedRecords -k HailHistory -k HailAddresses -k HailSwathLayers -k HailJoins -k SheetFiveSeasonsInTheBrowser, then the full suite (tail); Chromium (PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium) at 390 and 1280 px on a scratch build from the adopted store with every flag: the five cells (Billings 921,2149; Benchland 792,1998; the gate 797,1986; 753,2230; 920,1899) compared text for text with describe_summary (table, notes, partial line, every section and all its rows), the cells 602,1396 and 607,1428, no placeholder, zero off-site requests, the fetch list per tap; delete the build.

label: smoke
items: Smoke completion items (rulings D75 to D83; the store is the adopted combined store /home/user/hail-b5/out/combined/store): (1) The sheet reader follows the round-2 DOM: joins_sheet (near line 1459) and the summary reader read [data-hail='summary'] and [data-hail='sections'] (the table, its notes under it, the eleven sections in the fixed order with their rows, notes and roof groups; every row is in the DOM, D83(a); read textContent, never innerText, so rows behind the Show all control are compared too); check_sample_labels (near line 1717) covers all eleven section ids (the sample word on a sample build, none on a store build); the three-cell comparison covers the table and every section's text against summary.describe_summary on the same store; the budgets come from map.json (the phone budget is 700,000 bytes gzip after D82(b)). (2) R15: a --history run on a build without --hail-addresses fails readably (one named failure, no traceback). (3) Re-run tools/smoke_map.py with the CI flags (no --store) and tools/smoke_pages.py --history on a fresh build from the adopted store with every flag (--storm-layers --hail-history --hail-addresses --hail-store /home/user/hail-b5/out/combined/store), at 390 and 1280 px, and quote the full output; every remaining failure is named with its owner. (4) The workflow files parse; the tests of your files pass; report the measured figures (phone view bytes, largest tap file, map.json sizes) for the docs.
